# Getting Authorized {#sec-getting-started .unnumbered}

Databrary restricts access to non-public data. To access non-public data on Databrary, users **must** be authorized by their institution or be a supervised researcher of a Databrary authorized researcher.

Our [Data Ethics](../ethics/ethics.qmd) page contains information about Databrary's ethical framework.

Any person may browse and view Databrary's public materials consistent with the [Terms & Conditions of Use](/appendices/terms.qmd). You may only download materials if you are logged in to Databrary.

::: callout-note
If you do not complete the authorization process, but you have a registered account on Databrary, you will only be able to access **public** data on Databrary that are de-identified or have permission to be shared publicly.
:::

If you represent an **institution**, see [this section](/for-institutions/for-institutions.qmd) for information about how researchers gain access to Databrary via a formal process of institutional authorization.

If you meet the requirements to be an **authorized researcher**, see [this section](authorized-researchers.qmd) about how to start the authorization process with your institution.

If you do not meet the requirements to be an authorized researcher (e.g., you are a **research staff member, postdoc, graduate or undergraduate student**) see [this section](sponsored-researchers.qmd) for information about how to gain access to restricted data via your research supervisor.
